Authenticate remote reads under a URL prefix.

garry_http_auth.Rd

Registers an HTTP header, typically Authorization: Bearer <token>, that GDAL sends with every request to a URL starting with prefix. It applies on the host and on every garry daemon, including pools that garry_daemons() starts later. The header is scoped to the prefix, so a token for one provider never reaches another. Setting GDAL_HTTP_HEADERS in the environment instead sends it to every host garry reads from.

Usage

garry_http_auth(prefix, header, refresh = 1800)

Arguments

prefix

URL prefix, e.g. "https://catalog.maap.eo.esa.int/". A bare http(s):// prefix is registered in its /vsicurl/ form, which is how garry opens remote sources; other GDAL virtual file system prefixes are taken as given.

header

A header line (several lines joined by "\r\n"), a function returning one, or NULL to remove the prefix's header.

refresh

Seconds before a function header is called again. Ignored for a fixed header.

Value

Invisibly, the registered prefixes.

Details

For short-lived tokens, pass a function as header. It is called now, and again when a collect() starts once refresh seconds have passed; a changed header is pushed to every daemon. GDAL keeps the header a file was opened with until every handle on that file closes, so a change also closes garry's cached dataset handles in every process. Tokens refresh between runs, not during one: choose refresh so that a token outlives refresh plus your longest run.

Header values are never printed, and they do not appear in task logs or garry_task_report().

See also

garry_daemons(), garry_gdal_config()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# ESA MAAP: exchange an offline token for a 10 h access token
garry_http_auth(
  "https://catalog.maap.eo.esa.int/",
  function() paste("Authorization: Bearer", maap_access_token()),
  refresh = 3600
)
} # }
